brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A strip-shaped, part-baked and part-pan-fired green tea from the Ending tea farm and the Gushan and Guling area of Fuzhou, Fujian. Its name, white cloud, comes from its abundant white down.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: It sells mainly in Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Anhui and Shanghai. Little more is documented about it.
processing: Lightly withered, fixed at high heat, shaped, then baked slowly at low heat.
harvest_season: One bud with one just-opening leaf.
appearance_dry: Round, straight, full strips of jade green with visible down.
appearance_wet: Usually soft green leaf that opens up in the water.
taste_profile: Clear, high aroma and a fresh, brisk taste.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
